Welcome back to your weekly roundup of AI legislation!

This map shows the number of AI-related bills FPF is tracking in each state, including 2026 introductions, 2025 carryover bills, and select enacted laws from last year. Nearly every state is active: North Dakota is the only state not currently represented.

For suggestions for future call topics, please reach out to jfrancis@fpf.org. 

 

IYMI : New Resource on U.S. Privacy Enforcement in 2025: FPF released its 2025 U.S. Privacy Enforcement Report, highlighting four of the top enforcement trends of the last year. Check it out here! One of FPF's four key takeaways is the observation that the new FTC, led by Chair Ferguson, focused its enforcement actions and settlements on addressing deceptive claims about the capabilities of AI-enabled products. 

 

Highlights

 

  • Illinois bill introduction deadline passes: Illinois’ bill introduction deadline has passed, bringing 17 new AI bills across major categories this week, including data-driven pricing, transparency, employment, health, liability, chatbots, and frontier model safety.
  • California chatbot ballot initiative paused: OpenAI and Common Sense Media have paused their “Parents & Kids Safe AI Act” 2026 ballot campaign on chatbots to pursue legislation directly through the California Legislature.
  • Bills advancing through committee: 4 bills passed through committee in Hawaii pertaining to chatbots, transparency, and data-driven pricing and Virginia pertaining to employment, ADMT/ High-Risk AI, chatbots, and transparency. 
  • Bills advancing through first chamber: 2 bills passed through their first chamber in Virginia (SB 269 health and SB 384 transparency) and Mississippi (SB 2437, miscellaneous).
  • More in the tracker: As always, summaries of these bills, along with additional updates, are available in the FPF AI Legislation Tracker.


Stuff from the States

 

Arizona - Frontier Models/ High-Risk AI - HB 4098: Introduced by Rep. Travers (D), this bill would establish comprehensive risk assessment, transparency, and bias mitigation requirements for high risk AI systems, including evaluating the potential for discrimination or bias.

 

California - 

  • Transparency - SB 1000: Introduced by Sen. Becker (D), this bill would mandate that content generated by AI includes latent disclosures of data provenance that is “permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove.”
  • California - Chatbot Ballot Initiative Paused: OpenAI and Common Sense Media have announced that they are pausing their “Parents & Kids Safe AI Act” ballot campaign for 2026 in favor of passing legislation directly through the California Legislature this session. The coalition stated it hopes to work with lawmakers on a framework addressing age assurance, child safety risk assessments, parental controls, protections against harmful design, privacy safeguards, and independent audits. If legislative negotiations stall, the campaign has indicated it may revive the measure for the 2028 ballot.

 

Connecticut - Chatbot/Sandbox - SB 86: Introduced by Rep. Lemar (D), this bill would direct a state agency to develop a plan for a sandbox that tests innovative AI products and services under reduced regulatory requirements. The bill also requires companion chatbot platforms to implement safeguards for minors and include regular disclosures of the chatbot’s non-human status. 

 

Georgia - Liability - SB 488: Introduced by Sen. Setzler (R), this bill would classify generative AI systems as personal property for product liability cases involving minors, establishes liability for product sellers, and imposes a duty to warn of risks.

 

Hawaii - Four bills passed through committee this week: SB 3001 (chatbots), HB 2502 (chatbots), HB 2357 (transparency), and HB 2458 (data-driven pricing).

 

Illinois - The bill introduction deadline has now passed, bringing with it 17 additional AI-related bills introduced this week. 

  • Three bills on data-driven pricing: (HB 4985, HB 5323, SB 3657).
  • Four bills related to transparency: (HB 4988, SB 3454, SB 3601, SB 3364).
  • Two bills related to employment: (HB 4987 and SB 3571).
  • Two bills related to health: (HB 5284 and SB 3702).
  • Two bills related to liability:
    • SB 3502: Introduced by Sen. Ventura (D), this bill would establish product liability standards and accountability measures for developers and deployers of high-impact and generative AI systems.
    • SB 3590: Introduced by Sen. Edly-Allen (D), this bill would establish a legal framework for holding developers and deployers of high-impact and generative AI systems accountable for harm caused by their products.
  • Three bills related to chatbots: 
    • Chatbots/Liability - SB 3368: Introduced by Sen. Rezin (R), this bill would provide that chatbot deployers may not disclaim liability if the chatbot provides materially misleading or harmful information that results in financial loss or other demonstrable harm. 
    • Chatbots/Liability - HB 5044: Introduced by Rep. Gong-Gershowitz (D), this bill would designate chatbots as products subject to strict liability, making providers legally responsible for user injuries regardless of care or direct relationship. 
    • Chatbots - SB 3384: Introduced by Sen. Ellman (D), this bill would require AI companion operators to implement protocols for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation and to provide clear user notifications of the system’s non-human status. 
  • AI Safety/Frontier Models - SB 3444: Introduced by Sen. Cunningham (D), this bill would provide liability protections for developers of advanced AI models, contingent on the publication of safety protocols and transparency reports.

 

Kansas - Two new bills introduced on chatbots: (SB 499 and HB 2772).

 

Maryland - 

  • Chatbots - SB 827: Introduced by Sen. Hester (D), this bill would set comprehensive regulations for the design, deployment, and operation of chatbots, including setting consumer privacy protections. Among other requirements, this bill would prohibit operators from using chat logs for targeted advertising, profiling users beyond what is necessary to respond to prompts, and retaining chat logs for more than ten years.  Developers and operators would be required to implement robust data security programs, conduct monthly safety testing, and publicly disclose their findings. 
  • Bills were also introduced on health (HB 995), AI safety (HB 924), and chatbots (HB 952).

 

Mississippi - 

  • Misc - SB 2437 (defining “artificial intelligence” in Mississippi code) passed through the Senate.

 

Rhode Island -

  • ADMT/Employment - SB 2499: Introduced by Sen. Gu (D), this bill would create a comprehensive framework for the use of AI and electronic monitoring in the workplace, establishing strict limits, transparency requirements, and employee protections.
  • Health/Transparency - HB 7538: Introduced by Rep. Tanzi (D), this bill would require healthcare providers and facilities to notify patients whenever artificial intelligence is used to document their in-person or telehealth visits. 
  • Bills were also introduced on data-driven pricing (SB 2428) and transparency/GenAI (HB 7543).

 

South Carolina - Two new bills introduced on chatbots (SB 896 and HB 5138).

 

Tennessee -  Chatbots/Frontier Models - SB 2171: Introduced by Sen. Yager (R), this bill would require large AI developers and chatbot providers in Tennessee to implement, publish, and regularly update detailed safety and child protection plans. Comparable legislation was recently introduced in Nebraska (LB 1083), Utah (HB 286), Tennessee (HB 1898), and Illinois (HB 4705/ SB 3261).

 

Virginia - 

  • Two bills passed through the Senate: SB 269 (health; Illinois’ HB 1806-style bill) and SB 384 (transparency; creating frameworks for IVOs to audit AI systems).
  • Four bills passed through committee: HB 1514 (employment), HB 999 (ADMT/ High-Risk AI), HB 669 (chatbots), HB 713 (transparency).

 

Wisconsin - Chatbots - SB 939: Introduced by Sen. Jacque (R), this bill would establish strict safety requirements and enforcement mechanisms for AI companion chatbots interacting with children and includes a private right of action. 

 

Wyoming - Health/GenAI/ Liability - HB 102: Introduced by Rep. Lien (R), this bill would prohibit the development or distribution of AI systems intended to promote self-harm. Among other requirements, the bill would also create new criminal offenses for the development or distribution of CSAM. The bill also provides immunity to AI developers from liability for damages arising from the misuse of their systems by third parties, except when the developer should have known the system would be used for illegal purposes.

  • Maryland - HB 924 (AI Safety) and HB 712 (Liability) is set to be heard March 4 in the House Judiciary Committee.

  • South Dakota - Chatbots - SB 168 is set to be heard today Feb. 12 in the Senate Judiciary Committee.
